paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend. Your body is not a side issue. Paul says it is for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body (1 Corinthians 6:13). Your body isn't something to ignore until heaven, because God raised the Lord from the dead by His power, and "He will raise us also" (1 Corinthians 6:14).

Now look at the two "Everything is permissible for me" lines. Paul says "not everything is beneficial," and "I will not be mastered by anything" (1 Corinthians 6:12). So the question isn't only "Can I?" It's "Is this good for me, and who's running the show?" I've seen what happens when a habit grabs the apron strings, and that is a bad batch every time. Paul gives the church a short command here: "Flee from sexual immorality" (1 Corinthians 6:18). He says this sin is against your own body, and he reminds them that they are united with the Lord (1 Corinthians 6:15-18).

And here's why it all holds together. Your body is "a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you," and "You are not your own; you were bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). You aren't a free-floating baker doing whatever the oven allows. You belong to the One who paid for you, and the Holy Spirit lives in you. So Paul lands it with a "Therefore": "glorify God with your body" (1 Corinthians 6:20). Today, friend, that means you bring your body into your obedience, because it's His.
